3. During investigation of the case, the police of the concerned police station went to the place of occurrence and recorded the statements of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal of Procedure. However, having found no prima-facie case, the police submitted final report. No. 230 dated 28.5.2008 against the accused-petitioner and others. 

 4. Being aggrieved by the final report, the informant submitted a naraji petition before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhaka who passed an order for further investigation. Thereafter, the inspector of Police (D.B) took investigation of the case and having found prima-facie case, he submitted charge sheet No.52 dated 31.1.2009 against the accused-petitioner and others under sections 420/406/467/468/ 471/109/506 of the Penal Code. 

 7. At the very outset, Mr. Md. Habibullah, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that one Kuhimuddin and others as plaintiffs earlier filed Civil Suit No. 95 of 2003 for permanent injunction against the accused-petitioner before the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka and that judgment of above-mentioned suit ultimately went against the aforesaid plaintiffs and as such the present criminal proceeding filed by the informant over the self-same matter is not maintainable. He next submits that the allegations brought against the accused-petitioner are .totally false, fabricated, uncertain and unspecific and that those allegations do not disclose any offence against the accused-petitioner and as Such, the order of framing charge the petitioner under sections 420/467/468/471 is, wholly, ex-facie illegal and the impugned proceeding is an abuse Of process of the Court and as such, the impugned proceeding should be quashed. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr. Monjur Rader, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the State, submits that. FIR and other materials on record disclose prima-facie offences against' the petitioner and others under sections 420/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code and that the learned Additional Chief Judicial Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate rightly framed charge against the accused-petitioner under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code. He further submits that the allegations brought against the petitioner in the FIR are the factual matters which require to be proved by evidence. He lastly submits that there is no legal bar to filing a criminal case notwithstanding the fact that a civil suit is pending over a self-same matter and that the impugned proceeding cannot be quashed under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and as such, in view of the above facts and circumstances of the case, the Rule should be discharged. 

 11. Keeping in view the relevant provisions of law, we went to discuss and examine as to whether the F.I.R discloses a prima-facie offence of cheating and forgery against the petitioner in the instant case or not. On a plain reading of the FIR, it transpires to an that prima-facie, the accused-petitioner, in collusion with other accused, sold out the case land to Md. Rashidul Haque by a registered deed of sale being No. 8874 dated 14.5.2000, a valuable security, as a constituted attorney by virtue of power of attorney being No. 7848 dated 29.12.1986, after forging the alleged power of attorney dated 29.12.1986 though the petitioner was neither an executant nor a constituted attorney of the power of attorney dated 29.12.1986. Prima-facie it transpires further from F.I.R and other prosecution-materials that the petitioner, in collaboration with other accused, dishonestly and fraudulently sold out the land with an intention to obtain wrongful advantage for herself or to cause a legal injury or a possible legal injury to the informant. It appears from the F.I.R that there are prima-facie offences of cheating and forgery against the accused-petitioner and others under sections 420/467/468/471/ 109 of the Penal Code. Moreover,, the aforesaid allegation as disclosed in the F.I.R categorically admitted by the accused-petitioner in paragraph No.5 of supplementary affidavit dated 20.7.2011, wherein the petitioner stated very clearly that the deed writer inadvertently gave reference to the power of attorney being No. 7848 dated 29.12.1986 and wrongly introduced the petitioner as constituted attorney in the deed of sale dated 14.5.2000 by way of clerical mistake. It stems out from the aforesaid statements that the accused petitioner virtually admitted the allegations as alleged in the F.I.R. However, the story as to wrong entry of the petitioner's name as the constituted attorney in the deed of sale by clerical mistake is a matter of fact which requires to be proved by evidence. In this connection, we may refer to a decision in the case of Dr. M. Faruq Vs. The State and another ,16 BLD(AD) (1996) 51, wherein it has been decided; 

 Furthermore, it is a settled principle of law that if the F.I.R or the petition of complaint discloses prima facie allegations against the accused, those allegations are the matters of facts which are required to be decided by the Trial Court on taking evidence. The aforesaid legal view finds support in the case of Mr. Moudud Ahmed Vs. The State, 16 BLD (AD) (1996) 27, wherein it has been held that 

 "In exercising power under section 561 A, the High Court Division is only to see if there are prima-facie allegations disclosing criminal offences. The admissibility, relevance, Propriety or sufficiency of materials collected by the prosecution are matters for the trial court to decide on taking evidence as all these fall outside the ambit of section 242 and 561 A of the Code of Criminal procedure." 

 12. Now we want to discuss another ground taken by the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner that the one Kuhimuddin and others as plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit No. 95 of 2003 before the learned Assistant Judge. Damrai, Dhaka for permanent injunction against the accused-petitioner but the plaintiffs could not prove possession over the suit land and the suit was ultimately dismissed and as such, the impugned proceeding over the self-same matter is not maintainable. Though the plaintiffs categorically stated about the alleged power of attorney in the plaint of the suit, the learned Judge of the trial Court did not give any observation that the alleged power of attorney was forged and concocted one. 

 13. True it is that one Kuhimuddin and others as plaintiff filed Civil Suit No. 95 of 2003 before the learned Assistant Judge, Damrai Adalat, Dhaka for perpetual injunction and in that suit, the prima-facie issue was to determine the possession of the contending parties. Though the learned Judge categorically and incidentally discussed the power of attorney, that was not the fact in issue for adjudication in that suit. Over and above, the purpose of filing civil suit and criminal case is quite different and distinguishable from each other. If the F.I.R or prosecution-materials disclose prima-facie ingredients of offences against accused- petitioner, a criminal proceeding is maintainable in spite of the fact that a civil suit is pending over the self-same matter. In this connection, we may refer to a decision in the case of Khandaker Abul Bashar Vs State and another, 63 DLR (AD) (2011) 79 wherein it has been spelt out that: 

 14. In the instant case, it appears from the record of the case that no civil suit has been filed challenging the legality or propriety of the deed of sale allegedly executed and registered by the petitioner and others. It is not also a case of the petitioner that the informant as plaintiff earlier filed Civil Suit No. 95 of 2003 before the learned Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka against the petitioner and others for perpetual injunction. On a bare reading of the FIR we find that there is a prima-facie allegation of cheating and forgery against the petitioner who, in collusion with other accused, forged the power of attorney dated 29.12.1986 and sold out the case land to obtain wrongful advantage or to cause a legal injury to the informant impersonating herself as a constituted attorney. So, we find that there are prima-facie ingredients of cheating and forgery against the accused of the case. It is very much evident from the above-mentioned decision that there is no legal bar to filing a criminal case for the criminal liability and a civil suit for the civil liability. If, for the sake of argument, we hold that a civil suit has been filed challenging the legality and genuineness of the deed of sale, even then there is no bar to proceeding with the criminal case if the 'F.I.R or the petition of complaint discloses prima-facie allegations having ingredients of the offences against the accused notwithstanding the fact that a civil suit is pending over the self-same matter. 

 15. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the settled principle of law, we are of the view that the present case does not come within the ambit of principles of quashing the proceeding under section 56IA of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as the F.I.R discloses prima-facie ingredients of offences against the accused-petitioner and others under section 420/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code.
